# AI-Generated Format Requirements Pipeline

**Document type:** System design (normative)
**Authority level:** Normative — governs requirement generation for `generated-requirements/`
**Created:** 2026-05-13
**Human authorization:** Explicit (Babar Raza, 2026-05-13) — system-generated requirements required before implementation

---

## Core Principle

**Detailed per-format requirements must be generated by the system using AI, not manually authored.**

Human product goals define the target. The system generates detailed per-format requirements from:
- Local specifications (cached, provenance-verified)
- Normalized spec artifacts (tools/spec-normalize/)
- Format understanding layer (acquisition-packs/{format}/)
- Neutral model schemas (schemas/neutral-model/{format}/)
- Existing source and tests (src/net/{format}/, tests/net/{format}/)
- Product goals (docs/product-factory/commercial-product-capability-model.md)

---

## Human Product Goals (PRODUCT_DECISION — Immutable)

These come from human direction (Babar Raza, 2026-05-13) and are source_type: PRODUCT_DECISION:

1. Load supported format → build in-memory document object model
2. Inspect and manipulate the DOM programmatically
3. Edit format-specific entities in the DOM
4. Save same format with or without edits (round-trip)
5. Export/convert to PDF, PNG, HTML, and related family formats

---

## Input Sources (Ordered by Authority)

| Priority | Source | Location | Source Type |
|----------|--------|----------|-------------|
| 1 | Human product goals | This document + capability model | PRODUCT_DECISION |
| 2 | Verified facts | acquisition-packs/{format}/verified-facts.yaml | VERIFIED_FACT |
| 3 | Implementation requirements | acquisition-packs/{format}/implementation-requirements.yaml | VERIFIED_FACT |
| 4 | Neutral model schema | schemas/neutral-model/{format}/model.yaml + field-map.yaml | VERIFIED_FACT |
| 5 | Existing .NET source | src/net/{format}/*.cs, Model/*.cs | EXISTING_SOURCE |
| 6 | Existing .NET tests | tests/net/{format}/*.cs | TEST_EVIDENCE |
| 7 | Format profile | acquisition-packs/{format}/format-profile.yaml | VERIFIED_FACT |
| 8 | Tier map | acquisition-packs/{format}/tier-map.yaml | VERIFIED_FACT |
| 9 | Normalized spec text | .local/spec-normalize/{format}/text.txt | SPEC |
| 10 | Security surface | acquisition-packs/{format}/security-surface.yaml | VERIFIED_FACT |
| 11 | AI retrieval/synthesis | (LLM call over above sources) | AI_PROPOSAL |

---

## AI Pipeline Stages

```
Stage 1: INPUT COLLECTION
  ↓ Collect all input sources, compute hashes, verify existence

Stage 2: RETRIEVAL
  ↓ Query normalized spec text (Tier 1/2 lexical retrieval)
  ↓ Retrieve relevant sections by element name, attribute name

Stage 3: REQUIREMENT EXTRACTION
  ↓ For each product goal: extract relevant spec constraints
  ↓ Cross-reference with verified facts and neutral model
  ↓ Assign source_type and confidence

Stage 4: REQUIREMENT NORMALIZATION
  ↓ Assign unique requirement_id
  ↓ Map to capability_level (C0-C10)
  ↓ Map to product_goal
  ↓ Classify: load / edit / save / convert

Stage 5: OBJECT MODEL CANDIDATE GENERATION
  ↓ From verified facts + existing source: propose C# types
  ↓ Mark AI_PROPOSAL if not directly in existing source
  ↓ Validate against neutral model schema

Stage 6: SAVE/EDIT/CONVERSION REQUIREMENT GENERATION
  ↓ Derive edit requirements from object model
  ↓ Derive save requirements from load requirements (inverse)
  ↓ Mark conversion requirements as FUTURE_SCOPE

Stage 7: RISK AND GAP ANALYSIS
  ↓ Identify UNKNOWN items (no spec evidence)
  ↓ Identify conflicting requirements
  ↓ Classify items requiring human decision

Stage 8: VERIFIER REVIEW (Lane R5)
  ↓ Independent verifier challenges all generated requirements
  ↓ Classify: VERIFIED_ACCEPTED / REJECTED / REPAIR_REQUIRED

Stage 9: SCHEMA VALIDATION (Lane R2 validator)
  ↓ Validate against JSON schemas
  ↓ All required fields present
  ↓ Status constraints checked

Stage 10: ACCEPTANCE
  ↓ Mark ACCEPTED_FOR_VERTICAL_SLICE for implementable subset
  ↓ Gate: implementation lanes may only consume this subset
```

---

## Output Artifacts

Generated to `generated-requirements/{format}/`:

| File | Content |
|------|---------|
| commercial-requirements.yaml | All requirements, all categories |
| object-model-requirements.yaml | Entity type definitions |
| save-edit-requirements.yaml | Save, edit, round-trip requirements |
| conversion-requirements.yaml | Export/convert requirements (future-scoped) |
| traceability-map.yaml | Requirement ID → product goal + spec section |
| verifier-review.yaml | Verifier classifications per requirement |
| generation-report.md | Generation metadata, model used, input hashes |

---

## Validation Rules

1. Every requirement must map to a product goal
2. Every format-specific requirement must cite local evidence OR be marked PRODUCT_DECISION
3. UNKNOWN or NEEDS_REVIEW items must be clearly marked
4. AI_PROPOSAL requirements cannot be ACCEPTED without verifier approval
5. ACCEPTED_FOR_VERTICAL_SLICE requirements must have test_requirements defined
6. Conversion requirements must be future-scoped (not ACCEPTED_FOR_VERTICAL_SLICE in initial sprint)
7. Capability claims must not exceed evidence

---

## Repeatability Requirements

Every generation run must produce:
- `generator_version`: pipeline version
- `model_tool`: AI model/tool used (or AI_UNAVAILABLE)
- `input_source_hashes`: hash of each input file
- `generation_timestamp`: ISO 8601
- `spec_version`: "ODF 1.3"

Manual edits to generated files must be separated from pipeline output using `manually_edited: true` field.

Stale detection: If any input_source_hash changes, generated requirements must be regenerated.

---

## Implementation Gate

Implementation lanes (C-F) must not start until:
- Lane R1: LANE_R1_PASS
- Lane R2: LANE_R2_PASS (validator tests pass)
- Lane R3: LANE_R3_PASS or LANE_R3_PASS_WITH_LOW_CONFIDENCE_ITEMS
- Lane R4: LANE_R4_PASS or LANE_R4_PASS_WITH_LOW_CONFIDENCE_ITEMS
- Lane R5: LANE_R5_PASS or LANE_R5_PASS_WITH_NOTES
- Schema validation: PASS
- ACCEPTED_FOR_VERTICAL_SLICE requirements exist

If gate fails: `REQUIREMENTS_GENERATION_NOT_READY_FOR_IMPLEMENTATION`
